title: tools_plan output
description: Output for tools_plan. The proposals are DATA. Each carries the name and argument object the engine produced, plus the package's own verdict on it. There is deliberately no field an executable handle, a callback or a resolved tool could travel in: the object is closed, and the package exposes no dispatcher, so a caller that wants a call to happen must perform it itself.

proposals.description: Proposed calls whose name was offered AND whose arguments satisfy the offered tool's schema. Nothing here has been executed.

rejected.description: Proposed calls this package REFUSED to pass through, each with the reason. Reported rather than dropped: a silently discarded proposal looks identical to a model that proposed nothing.

suppressed.description: Calls the ENGINE withheld, carried through so a caller sees the same suppression the engine applied.

reasoning.description: The engine's own stated reasoning for the turn. It is the model's account of itself, not a verified explanation.

confidence.description: The engine's self-reported confidence. It is not a calibrated probability and must not be presented as one.

grounding.description: The engine's grounding report, passed through unchanged. `ungrounded` names values the engine could not tie to the input.

arguments.description: The argument object the engine produced, verbatim. It is data only.

offered.description: Whether the name was in the caller's offered set. False means the engine produced a name the caller never declared.

valid.description: Whether the arguments satisfy the offered tool's declared schema. A well-formed call is not necessarily a correct one.

issues.description: Every argument violation found, so a caller can see the whole report rather than the first problem.

meta.description: The host stamps this envelope. The provider never authors it (EXT-17).
